title: This lint warns about the use of literals as write!/writeln! args.
summary: Using literals as writeln! args is inefficient (c.f., https://github.com/matthiaskrgr/rust-str-bench) and unnecessary (i.e., just put the literal in the format string) Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This lint warns when you use write!() with a format string that ends in a newline.
summary: You should use writeln!() instead, which appends the newline. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: This lint warns when you use writeln!(buf, "") to print a newline.
summary: You should use writeln!(buf), which is simpler. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for methods with certain name prefixes or suffixes, and which do not adhere to standard conventions regarding how self is taken.
summary: The actual rules are: Consistency breeds readability. If you follow the conventions, your users won’t be surprised that they, e.g., need to supply a mutable reference to a as_.. function. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmutes that can’t ever be correct on any architecture.
summary: It’s basically guaranteed to be undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.
